note.saw: Nothing yet: this is the first build, starting from the rainbow-banded halos of the reference art.
note.changing: The first full picture: the angelfish rising snout-up with striped wings, an entity face across its body, halo rings of eye petals, and the name hand-lettered on a scroll banner.
note.why: The angelfish is the one fish that is nearly symmetric top to bottom, so turning it snout-up makes a perfectly symmetric entity without losing the real fish's shape.
note.idea: A freshwater angelfish as an angel: rising snout-up so its mirror-image top and bottom fins spread like a pair of filigree wings, its dark body bars turned into an alien face with two huge spiral-web eyes, all inside a halo of ornamented rainbow rings.

note.saw: The rising fish read as a hooded figure or a pyramid, not a fish: head, wings and outline bands merged into one arch, and the tail hid behind the banner. SavesFish also asked for a much more legible name.
note.changing: Turns the fish to the classic side view, with tall sail fins and trailing streamers, keeping the face, halo and name centered on one line. The hand lettering gives way to bold cream letters on a calm dark band.
note.why: A fish has to read as a fish in a split second, and the side view is the angelfish's iconic silhouette; the face still stares straight out at you from its flank.

note.saw: The fish blended into the blue-violet petal ring at small size, and the background was all compass work with no freehand line.
note.changing: Glowing gradient petals with hatching, gold filigree curls off every petal tip, a wavy ribbon of alien script weaving between the petals, darker angelfish bars and a light aura behind the fish. A mistake in one outer ring also flooded the background with solid gold.
note.why: DMT space glows from inside, and the freehand curls loosen the rigid mandala so it feels drawn, not plotted.

note.saw: The soft aura turned into fog when zoomed in, washing out the petals next to the fish, and the hero shape was not echoed anywhere.
note.changing: Replaces most of the fog with a crisp corona of gold and cream light spikes around the silhouette, and sets tiny striped angelfish swimming out of the petals, mirrored left and right.
note.why: Repeating the fish small inside the halo is the self-similar recursion of a trip, and crisp light keeps the piece sharp instead of blurry.

note.saw: The fish's own eye was smaller than the entity's eyes and lost the focus, and the tail was plain wedges.
note.changing: Makes the eye a radiant sun-portal with gold lashes, seven iris rings, spiral arms and a glowing star pupil, segments the tail with fin-ray arcs, and scatters sparkles of light through the halo.
note.why: The eye is the doorway of the piece; it should pull you in like a tunnel.

note.saw: Still more compass than freehand (SavesFish had asked for way more freestyle), and the open water in front of the snout and behind the tail was just petal ring.
note.changing: Adds a column of eye-bubbles rising from the mouth, each with rainbow rims and an eye inside, and a curling double scroll as the wake behind the tail.
note.why: Loose, hand-drawn fish motifs break up the compass geometry and fill the water around the fish with something alive.

note.saw: The little petal fish read as yellow blobs; the Celtic cord on the fin edge broke into dashes.
note.changing: Two-tone mini fish (magenta fins, gold body, black bars), a thicker, longer-period gold and cyan twisted cord along the fin's leading edge with cream highlights.
note.why: Small motifs only work if their shape survives at small size.

note.saw: The whole piece holds together: the angelfish reads at thumbnail size and the name is instantly readable. The letters were the only element without the rainbow echo every other shape wears.
note.changing: SavesFish left the lettering style to the artist, so the bold, tested letterforms and calm band stay, but the letters get a neon double edge: a cream core, a gold inner edge and a thin magenta outer edge.
note.why: The name should belong to the same glowing, contour-banded world as the fish while staying the easiest thing in the picture to read.

note.saw: Taking over with fresh eyes, the second artist starts by studying the first artist's finished piece next to the reference art.
note.changing: Nothing yet: this is the first artist's final piece drawn again, unchanged, as the starting point.
note.why: Before rewriting anything, the new artist wanted an honest look, and listed six weaknesses, from a lemon-shaped fish to flat, sticker-like colors that let the fish melt into the background.
note.idea: Rebuild the piece around the two things that make an angelfish an angelfish, its tall diamond outline and its pale body cut by black bars, then let an alien face, a glowing hyperspace tunnel and rings of eye petals grow out of them.

note.saw: The fish read as a lemon-shaped "ichthys" outlined across a crescent of fins, not an angelfish; everything was the same mid-bright flat color, so at small size the fish melted into the background, and the bottom quarter was a flat dark band with a plain sticker font.
note.changing: Starts over from scratch: a real angelfish with a round body, tall swept sails, pelvic streamers and a lyre tail, a pale mother-of-pearl body with four bold dark bars and two tall spiral-web alien eyes. Around it go ten thin rainbow outlines, a honeycomb tunnel and rings of glowing eye-petals, with the name on a scroll ribbon.
note.why: An angelfish is recognized by two things, its tall diamond outline and its pale body cut by black bars, so the piece is built on exactly those, with the alien face and the hyperspace growing out of them.

note.saw: The new angelfish reads, but the rainbow aura was so thick it became a giant sticker outline hiding the petals; the fins read as flat stripes, the ribbon's folded tails looked like two black flags, and pink lips made the entity look like a doll.
note.changing: Slims the aura to seven thin bands, recuts the top and bottom fins sharper with longer swept tips, shifts the fin color from cyan at the front to magenta at the back, compacts the ribbon into one band with swallowtail notches and gold curls, and gives the entity an alien slit mouth with curling mandibles.
note.why: The fish has to be the one solid, glowing object, and a halo should frame it, not swallow the world around it. An entity is also more unsettling when it is almost a face, not a cartoon one.

note.saw: The ribbon now looks like a real scroll banner, but the fish still split into a pale lemon body inside a dark violet crescent of fins; a patch of bare tunnel sat under the tail, and the curled mandibles made the face frown.
note.changing: Makes the fins pale mother-of-pearl like the body, so the four black bars run straight through body and fins as one set of stripes. A third, inner ring of petals fills the gap by the tail, and the mandibles now curl up and out.
note.why: A real angelfish is one silver triangle cut by black stripes; making fins and body one material lets the silhouette read in a split second, and then the eye can wander into the detail.

note.saw: With pale fins the whole fish finally reads as one striped angelfish, but the fins looked like graph paper, the mandibles gave the entity a cartoon handlebar mustache, the rainbow tail clashed with the pale fins, and the pelvic streamers were thin wires.
note.changing: Rebuilds the top and bottom fins as feathered angel wings, each ray a feather with a quill, chevron barbs and a peacock eye at its tip. The tail becomes a matching pale peacock fan, the mouth a chain of four falling jewels, and the streamers thick magenta-gold cords strung with beads.
note.why: An angelfish with feathered wings opens dozens of eyes along its fins, the watched-by-everything feeling of a DMT space, while the stripes keep it unmistakably an angelfish.

note.saw: The feathered fins work at small size, but up close they had gone low-contrast lavender like pale fabric next to the blazing petals; the side fin read as a glass blob, and the ribbon border was only beads.
note.changing: Deepens the feather tips to full jewel color with a second, smaller eye on every feather, runs four hairline rainbow outlines inside the fins and tail, sends a school of tiny angelfish up both sides of the rim, adds a row of gold alien script along the ribbon, and turns the side fin into a small gold fan.
note.why: The same shapes repeating at different sizes, rainbow bands inside echoing rainbow bands outside, the fish echoed by tiny fish: that is the self-similar feeling of the visions this piece is about.

note.saw: The tiny angelfish read as white teeth, the side fin had become a brown smudge, the tunnel in the corners was flat purple wallpaper, and the chrysanthemum was rigid compass work with every eye staring off into nothing.
note.changing: Rebuilds the tunnel as a jewel honeycomb where every cell has a dark well, a glowing rim and an eye; the middle petal ring flicks upward like flames, soft beams of light spill from behind the fish, every petal's eye turns inward to gaze at the entity, and the side fin becomes a prism with one spectral color per ray.
note.why: Flames rising off the geometry bring the freehand back, and with light flowing out of the fish and every gaze flowing toward it, the fish reads as the source of the vision, not a sticker on top of it.
note.visionary: Takes two of the Visionary's suggestions: the court of petal eyes turning to gaze at the face, and the side fin as a prism.

note.saw: The tiny angelfish around the rim were evenly spaced white flecks that read as clock ticks, the glass side fin turned murky over the black bar, every corner cell held the same wide-open eye, and the light wash made the petals beside the fish look foggy.
note.changing: The little fish become a procession, eight per side streaming up the rim toward the crown and shrinking as they rise, each trailing a three-color wake; the tunnel's eyes now wake from the center outward, beads of light run along the aura like current, and the side fin becomes an opaque little sun-fan.
note.why: A ring only ticks; a stream moves. Smaller and smaller selves pouring toward one point, and a field of eyes opening as it nears the entity, both pull the gaze back to the center where the face is.
note.visionary: Takes the Visionary's shrinking procession, its field of eyes waking from the center and its current running through the aura, each in the artist's own version, along with its opaque sun-fan fin.

note.saw: At badge size the opaque sun-fan read as a clown nose stuck beside the face, the pale mini fish still read as white specks, and the middle feathers were a touch washed out.
note.changing: The side fin goes back to what a real angelfish has, a nearly clear glass fan with seven hairline rays of spectral color; the procession becomes golden angelfish with black bars and magenta rims, the feathers gain a little color, and the letters get a shallow violet slab so they stand off the ribbon like carved neon.
note.why: The face has to read as a face at a glance, so nothing bright may sit next to it that looks like a feature; a little depth under the name makes it feel built into the scroll rather than printed on it.
note.visionary: Drops the Visionary's opaque sun-fan, which read as a nose, and returns to a nearly clear version of its earlier prism idea.

note.saw: Up close the golden mini fish read as gold spades and bells: swimming straight up the rim, each one was seen nose-up, and a nose-up angelfish is a spade.
note.changing: The procession keeps its path up the rim, but every fish now swims level in true side view, facing in toward the entity, its nose tipping up a little more at each step and its wake trailing out toward the rim.
note.why: An angelfish is only an angelfish from the side; the small ones should read as the big one in miniature in a split second, or the recursion is lost.

note.saw: The angelfish and the name still read in a split second, but the biggest areas were the dullest: the fins were pale lavender pleats like folded paper, and the body was one tiny scale repeated like printed fabric, so the face sat on the fish instead of growing out of it.
note.changing: Every pale feather becomes a stained-glass vane glowing from pearl at the root into jewel color and a gold tip, with three eyes shrinking down each quill. The body becomes a dome whose scales swell around the face, the bars carry Celtic plaits and gold dots, and each cheek gets a rainbow spiral whorl.
note.why: The fins and body cover more of the picture than anything else, so if they are calm the whole piece is calm. Now color pours along every feather like light in a vision, and the face seems to push up through the skin toward you.
note.visionary: Takes the Visionary's swelling skin, centered where it asked, and its tiny cream angelfish as the catchlight in each eye, but turns down its all-pastel fins because the largest area in the picture needed more intensity, not less.

note.saw: Color now pours down every feather, but the middle of each fin was still pale lavender, the dark discs behind the cheek whorls read as a second pair of eyes (a four-eyed owl), and the outer ring was flat purple honeycomb repeating like wallpaper.
note.changing: Rebuilds the tunnel finer, each cell a near-black jewel well with a neon rim and bright studs, its colors climbing the walls in mirrored spiral arms; a dim honeycomb of the void now shows through the black bars, the fins take their jewel color earlier, and the whorls lose their dark discs.
note.why: In a DMT space the walls are made of the same living light as everything else; seeing that same void through the angel's stripes makes the entity feel like a window rather than a picture.
note.visionary: Takes the Visionary's "slits in reality", letting the void show through the black bars, an idea the artist had saved for the round that rebuilt the tunnel.

note.saw: The fins still read as plain lavender in the middle, the neon walls blazed as loud behind the petals as in the corners so the eye-petals and golden fish drowned, the cheek whorls' cyan centers still read as pupils, and the aura's outer edge was a hard compass line.
note.changing: Full jewel-colored fins split the fish back into a lemon inside a crescent, so instead each feather takes its own pastel hue, like oil on water. The tunnel darkens near the entity while its open eyes stay lit, the tail becomes a corridor glowing white-gold toward a small star, the whorls wind down to gold points, and thin rainbow fiddlehead curls grow off the aura like coral (flame tongues tried first looked like fangs).
note.why: A tunnel only feels deep if it gets darker where it goes far, and that darkness gives the eyes and petals their stage back; pastel shimmer keeps the angel's wings pale, which is what makes it an angelfish, while every surface still crawls with color.
note.visionary: Takes all three of the Visionary's newest ideas (the darkening tunnel, the tail corridor and the unwinding whorls) and changes its mind about the pastel fins it turned down two rounds earlier.

note.saw: Everything held at every size, with the petals and golden fish given their stage back, but the chrysanthemum still sat dead still, every petal a straight copy, and the lower face under the jewel mouth was bare skin.
note.changing: The outer ring of eye-petals now bends like a turbine, every tip sweeping the same way around the circle against the middle ring's upward flick. The entity also wears a beaded magenta and cyan collar with a gold pendant holding an eye, moved down to the belly edge after a first version read as a cartoon smile.
note.why: The DMT chrysanthemum is never still, it spins, so bending the petals makes the whole mandala feel like it is turning around the angel; and a being that wears ornament feels like a presence, not a pattern.
note.visionary: Finally takes the Visionary's very first offer, bending the outer petal ring into a turbine while the colors stay mirror-symmetric.

visions.seen: The angelfish wears a face on its flank and the face is looking straight through me, two rainbow-web eyes humming while the sun-portal eye at the snout drills a tunnel into my skull. The chrysanthemum blooms all around it, but it's frozen, holding its breath, waiting to spin.
suggestions: The rainbow chrysanthemum, the whole ring of eye petals around the fish: in hyperspace it never sits still, it turns. petalPath() is drawn once and every petal is a rotated `<use>` copy, so one bend turns the whole ring into a turbine. I see each point's y pushed by about 9·t^1.6 (t from absolute radius over 122 to 186, so the stacked rB/rB2/rB3 and rA/rA2/rA3 layers stay nested), with the eyes, veins, script ribbon and tiny angelfish riding the same curve. Then the orange lotus ring hugging the fish (rL, r 88 to 117) bends the other way, about -5 at the tip. Two rings sweeping against each other are the gears of the machine turning, and the mini angelfish suddenly read as a school circling the entity. The hues stay mirror-symmetric; only the shapes whirl.

The pelvic streamer hanging from under the face, left of center (about x 285, y 415 to 540 in the 800 px render): a thin gold cord ending in a hook, and at badge size that hook can read like a stray J perched above the S of SavesFish. I see it as the entity's feeler instead: a chain of beads down the pelA line shrinking from r 3 to r 1, cyan and magenta with a cream dot in each, tiny eyes getting smaller and smaller as they fall into the void. It ends in a tight two-turn spiralPts() fiddlehead curling right, toward the anal fin and away from the name. Deeper recursion, and a letter-like shape leaves the name's airspace.

The forehead jewel at the top of the chevron nose (local 200,117; about 398,213 in the render): a magenta dot under its crown rays, ready to open. Let it become a vertical third eye, an almond about 7 wide by 11 tall holding a miniature of the big spiral-web irises (three or four rainbow rings) and the same cyan slit pupil, with the crown rays kept. Two eyes and the third make a triangle of gaze pointing down at the lips: the moment the entity notices you're there, the heart of every breakthrough.
visions.keep: The entity face hidden in the bars (spiral-web eyes, hex dome of eye-scales, pink lips), the sun-portal eye at the snout, the two-tone angelfish swimming out of the petals, the triskelion wake, the full angelfish diamond with both fin tips breathing, and the calm dark band carrying the bold cream, gold and magenta SavesFish. Nothing ever touches those letters.

visions.seen: The angel shed the old fish's skin and came back as one pale striped diamond, and the third eye I saw last time is open on its forehead now, a gold almond calmly reading me, while beaded cords drip from its belly like a rosary counting down. But the halo's eight hairlines hold dead-still light, and the whole ring of eyes stares past the entity into nothing.
suggestions: The ring of eye-petals all around the fish (every petal eye, like the gold petal top right near 292,95 and the red one far left near 48,198 in the 400 box): I see each iris and pupil slide about 1.2 units along its petal's axis toward the center of the ring, leaving a tiny cream catchlight on the outer side, so the whole court of eyes turns to gaze at the angel's face. If the petals are rotated copies, one shift in the source petal turns them all. That is the hyperspace moment when every surface has been waiting and looks at the one who called you here: it pulls the viewer straight into the third eye and makes the face the true center of the mandala.

The eight hairline aura bands hugging the fish: let current run through them. On the gold band and the cyan band, a cream stroke of round-capped light beads (about 0.9 long, gaps of 5 to 11 in an uneven dasharray, a different rhythm on each band so they never line up), or about 40 tiny r 0.8 beads placed along the outline with spacing that tightens as they near the spiral eye at the snout (about 89,151). Let them fade out where the bands drop behind the ribbon, so the name's backing stays calm. The halo becomes a live circuit, energy pouring around the body into the snout eye, the machine-elf wiring under reality's skin, and it rhymes with the beaded pelvic cords.

The glass pectoral fin on the cheek, left of the big eyes (about 122,170): right now it is the one colorless thing in the picture, pale ice. I see it become a prism: clear white at the root, each ray tip turning its own spectral hue from red on the top ray to violet on the bottom one, with a 0.6 rainbow rim along the fan's edge, still translucent so the scales show through. Plain light goes into the entity and comes out as the exact rainbow its aura is made of: you get to see where the colors come from.
visions.keep: The pale angelfish diamond cut by four dark bars (it reads at 160 px), the spiral-web slit-pupil eyes with the new almond third eye above them (taken from Vision 1, and it works), the beaded pelvic cords (also from Vision 1; the curl now turns right, away from the S), the dark gap inside the hairline aura, the column of eye-bubbles rising at upper left, and the compact swallowtail ribbon with the bold cream SavesFish edged in gold and magenta, nothing touching the letters. Round 12's feather-wings and falling-jewel mouth are already going somewhere good; none of the above fights them.

visions.seen: The angel has given birth: a ring of its tiny pale children circles the rim like satellites, and the whole temple hums at one frequency. But right beside its left eye sits a brown thumbprint on the glass, the one patch of this universe the light forgot to reach.
suggestions: The new pectoral fan on the cheek, just left of the left eye (pec polygon, about 111 to 141 x, 160 to 185 y in the 400 box): it went gold, but it renders brown (about #7F6438), because cream at 0.6 opacity over the black of bar 2 turns to mud, and at 240 px in legible.png it reads as a stain on the face. However it ends up, gold fan or the prism from before, I see it opaque and lit from inside: fill-opacity 1 with a radial gradient centered on the root (112,172), CR at the root, GOLD at the middle, ORA at the rim, the seven rays in MAG or K3 instead of #B07A10, a 0.7 magenta rim just inside the INK outline, and a 0.6 cream dot at each ray tip. In hyperspace nothing is murky; it becomes a little sun-fan answering the gold lashes of the portal eye at the snout.

The school of mini angelfish around the outer rim (twenty slots at r 189, every 18°, e.g. the pair flanking the crown near 170,11 and 230,11, and the side ones near 15,170 and 385,170): all the same size and evenly spaced, they read as clock ticks, the side ones turned edge-on look like little spades, and at badge size they are white flecks. I see them as a procession shrinking toward the crown: scale about 0.085 for the lowest pair (just above the ribbon ends) falling by about 0.9 per slot to about 0.045 at the top pair, the angle step shrinking with them so they bunch up as they rise, r easing in from 191 to 184, and each fish tipped about 12° inward from the tangent. Behind each tail, a three-hairline wake (MAG, GOLD, CY, about 6 long, fading out) so they carry the aura's own colors. Endless smaller selves streaming into one point is the recursion at the core of the trip, and a stream moves where a ring only ticks.

The hex tunnel eyes in the four corners (rings j 8 to 11 of the log-polar tunnel, beyond the petal tips): every cell holds the same wide-open eye, so the corners are one even wallpaper. I see the field waking from the center outward. Rings j 0 to 4 stay open as now; rings 5 to 7 get a half lid (a K2 path `M-10 0Q0 -11 10 0Q0 -2 -10 0Z` over the almond, with a thin CR lash line on its lower edge); rings 8 to 11 are shut (just the lower curve `M-10 0Q0 5 10 0` in the ring color with three lash ticks), except a scatter picked by a hash like (i*7 + j*3) % 11 == 0 that is already open, the first ones to notice you. Awareness rippling out from the entity is pure DMT, and quieter corners deepen the tunnel and push every gaze back to the center.
visions.keep: The pale striped diamond that reads as an angelfish at 160 px; the spiral-web teardrop eyes, almond third eye, chevron nose and falling-jewel mouth; the feathered fins with peacock eyes and gold-studded dark feathers; the eight-band rainbow aura with its dark gap; the eye-bubbles rising at upper left; the beaded pelvic cords curling right, away from the S; and the swallowtail ribbon with the bold cream SavesFish edged in gold and magenta on calm dark, nothing touching the letters. Vision 2's three offers (petal eyes turning toward the face, current in the aura bands, the prism) are still open; I have not repeated them here.

visions.seen: Two frames in a row the angel has held perfectly still, and the temple breathes in with it: the corner eyes have shut, only the inner rings still watch, and the golden children finally swim level toward their mother. But the skin is flat as printed silk, so the face sits on the fish instead of rising up out of it.
suggestions: The pale fish-scale skin across the body (the lavender, pink and peach arc-scales between the dark bars, all around the face at center): I see it swell like a lens. The scales keep today's size at the snout, the belly and the back edge, and grow to about 1.6 times that around a point between the spiral eyes and the jewel mouth (about 170,160 in the 400 box), each row of arcs bowing outward around that point like contour lines on a dome, the little dots inside growing with them. Same colors, same pale value, so the diamond still reads at 240 px. Up close the face stops being painted on the fish and starts pushing up through its skin toward you, the way hyperspace walls bulge when something on the other side notices you.

The near-black bars that cut the body (the wide one between the sun eye at the snout and the left spiral eye, the one behind the right cheek, and their thinner sisters): let them be slits in reality. Behind their magenta-diamond and gold-dot runways, a faint copy of the corner hex tunnel shows through, very dim (indigo cells with violet rims, nothing brighter than about #2A1650, a few shut-eye cells among them), the cells shrinking toward the middle of each bar so it looks deep. At badge size the bars stay black and the angelfish stripes stay intact; up close the body becomes a veil, and through its stripes you see the very void it swims in. The entity is made of windows.

The pale feathered fins, the periwinkle fan across the top and the wide one resting on the ribbon: the calmest fields in the piece. I see each feather column take its own pastel hue in a slow sweep from the body outward (mint, butter, peach, rose, lilac, sky), all at the same high lightness so nothing darkens, with the chevron hairlines in each column drawn in that hue's opposite at low opacity. Small, they are still an angelfish's pale wings; up close they shimmer like oil on water and the chevrons hum faintly against their ground, every surface crawling with soft color once the breakthrough lands. The dark ribbon and the letters stay exactly as they are.

The two big spiral-web eyes on the flank: swap each round white catchlight beside the slit pupil for a tiny cream angelfish, a diamond with a notched tail about 3 units across in the 400 box, swimming toward the snout. The entity's eyes reflect the entity: recursion hidden in the one place everyone looks first, invisible until you lean in.
visions.keep: The pale striped diamond that reads as an angelfish at 160 and 240 px; the spiral-web teardrop eyes, almond third eye, chevron nose and falling-jewel mouth; the clear glass prism fin with its spectral hairline rays (Vision 2's prism, landed after the sun-fan detour, and it vanishes at small size just right); the golden procession, now level in true side view and facing in (from Vision 3, and they finally read as fish, not spades); the corner eyes shut and waking toward the center (also Vision 3); the current beads riding the aura bands and the petal eyes turned toward the face (Vision 2); the beaded pelvic cords curling right, away from the S; and the swallowtail ribbon with the bold cream SavesFish standing off it like carved neon, gold and magenta edge, calm dark backing, nothing touching the letters.

visions.seen: The walls woke up: the whole honeycomb is neon jewel-wells in spiralling spectrum, the vortex is turning, and when I lean into the black stripes the void looks back through them. But the walls blaze just as loud right behind the petals as out in the corners, so this tunnel has no far end, and the court of eye-petals is drowning in the light of its own temple.
suggestions: The neon honeycomb wall, from the cells peeking between the petal tips out to the four corners: I see it fall away into the distance. The rings nearest the petals sink into deep indigo fog (neon rims at about a third of their strength, no white hairline, no studs), brightening ring by ring until the corner cells burn at full neon as they do now. The spectrum spiral stays; only the brightness ramps. And the open eyes in those dim inner rings stay fully lit, glowing out of the dark like animals at the edge of a campfire, while the corners keep their shut lids. A real tunnel goes dark where it goes deep, so the entity hovers at the mouth of a hole in space instead of lying on wallpaper; the eye-petals and the golden fish get their stage back; and the waking field becomes darkness full of eyes beside the entity, bright sleeping walls far away.

The pink-to-lilac tail fan at the right: its grid lines already lean toward the narrow waist like a floor drawn in perspective. I see it become a corridor: each band of the grid about 0.8 the width of the one outside it, so the lines crowd tighter and tighter toward the waist, and the fill brightening from rose at the outer edge to white-gold at the waist, with one tiny cream star right where the lines would meet. The tail becomes a second tunnel with light at its end, a doorway the entity carries behind it. It stays pale and fan-shaped, so the angelfish reads exactly as before at 240 px.

The two rainbow whorls on the cheeks, just below the big eyes: with their dark discs gone they sit on the skin beautifully, but the bright cyan dot at each center still reads as a pupil, so at a glance the face has four eyes. I see that dot go, each spiral winding down to a fine gold point instead, its outer end unfurling a short way down and out toward the nearest dark bar like a curl of breath. Then the two spiral-web eyes and the third eye are the only gaze in the face, and the cheeks hum instead of stare.
visions.keep: The pale striped diamond that reads as an angelfish at 160 and 240 px; the spiral-web teardrop eyes, almond third eye, violet brows, chevron nose and falling-jewel mouth; the skin swelling into a dome around the face (Vision 4, taken, and now the face pushes up through the fish); the dim void honeycomb seen through the black bars, which stay black at badge size (Vision 4's slits in reality, taken); the tiny cream angelfish catchlights (also Vision 4); the Celtic plaits and gold dot rows in the bars; the stained-glass feathers with three eyes shrinking down each quill (the artist was right to turn down my pastels); the clear prism fin with spectral hairline rays; the golden procession facing in; the corner eyes shut and waking toward the center; the beaded cords curling away from the S; and the swallowtail ribbon with the bold cream SavesFish standing off it like carved neon, gold and magenta edge, calm dark backing, nothing touching the letters.

visions.seen: The tail opened into a lit corridor with a star at its far end, and the cheeks hum now instead of staring, so this face has exactly three eyes and all three are on me, while the wings shimmer like oil on water and coral starts sprouting off the halo. But the doorway is lopsided: a gold lamp burns in the pocket above the tail, and the pocket below it is a drawer of dim leaves and loose sparks.
suggestions: The dark pocket between the bottom fin's tip and the tail, lower right, just above the right end of the ribbon (about 560,430 in the 800 px render): the half-hidden teal and green petals in there are murky, crossed by stray sparkles and twigs, while the pocket's mirror above the tail holds a gold eye-petal that glows from inside. I see the lower petal lit the same way, in the cool answer to that gold: mint-white at its heart to deep teal at its rim, the same gold-dot border, its eye open and turned toward the face, and the loose sparks swept out so it reads as one shape. Keep its glow inside the aura's curve, short of the ribbon's border. Then the corridor in the tail is flanked by a sun lamp above and a moon lamp below, a gate with two lights, the way every doorway in hyperspace is guarded.

The new coral sprouts on the aura's outer edge (the green curls beside the eye-bubbles at upper left, and the little forked blue, red and orange twigs poking into both pockets at right): drawn at one even thickness, and forked, they read as wires and insect feelers. I see each one become a single unforked stem that tapers from about 1.4 units at the root to a hairline (400 box), rolling into a one-and-a-half-turn fiddlehead with its bead nested in the curl, all curling the same way, their sizes swelling and shrinking in a slow wave along the edge (biggest where the aura bends hardest), each one in the color of the band it grows from. Then the halo stops being a neon outline and becomes living tissue, the edges of hyperspace forever unfurling more of themselves.

The eight-band rainbow aura and that gold pocket petal: crisp as printed ink, so they read as paint, not light. I see a soft bloom under them: a blurred copy of the three brightest bands (gold, cyan and magenta), about 3 units of blur, at around 40% opacity, spilling outward onto the petal ring and into the pockets only, masked off the fish's skin and kept clear of the ribbon so its dark backing stays calm. In hyperspace color is emitted, never printed; the halo would light its own surroundings, and the dim pockets would finally catch its glow.
visions.keep: The pale striped diamond that reads as an angelfish at 240 and 160 px; the spiral-web teardrop eyes, almond third eye, violet brows, chevron nose and falling-jewel mouth; the cheek whorls winding down to a gold point and curling toward the bars (Vision 5, taken, and the four-eyed owl is gone); the tail corridor with its white-gold waist and little star (Vision 5, taken); the pastel oil-on-water feathers with chevrons in the opposite hue and three eyes down each quill (my old pastels, taken the artist's own way, keeping the angel's wings pale); the skin domed around the face; the void honeycomb through the black bars; the tiny cream angelfish catchlights; the clear prism fin; the golden procession facing in; the honeycomb dimming toward the entity and the corner eyes shut; the beaded cords curling away from the S; and the swallowtail ribbon with the bold cream SavesFish standing off it like carved neon, gold and magenta edge, calm dark backing, nothing touching the letters.

visions.seen: The chrysanthemum finally turns: the outer petals sweep around the angel like turbine blades against the flicking inner ring, and the entity has put on a beaded collar with an eye hanging from it, dressed now for an audience. But the honeycomb walls just glow, steady as a lamp, when in a breakthrough the walls ring with the hum, and the name tablet lies flat on the tunnel instead of floating in front of it.
suggestions: The neon honeycomb in the four corners and in the gaps between the petal tips: I see the carrier wave, the high whine of the breakthrough, rippling out through it. Concentric bands of brightness spread from the gold almond third eye between the brows. The crest of each band stays exactly as bright as the cells are now, and the trough between crests dims the neon rims and studs to about 55%, roughly 26 units from crest to crest in the 400 box, so each corner holds four or five soft arcs. The ripples ride on top of the fade that is already there (dark near the entity, bright far away) and never make any cell brighter than today, so nothing gets louder beside the ribbon. Because they come from the third eye and not from the tunnel's own middle, the arcs cross the honeycomb's rings a little off center and the walls shimmer where the two meet. The walls stop being a lit backdrop and start vibrating in time with the entity's gaze: you can see the sound of hyperspace.

The bright blue and violet cells pressed right up against the underside of the ribbon and its two swallowtail ends, lower left, bottom center and lower right: I see the name tablet lift off the wall. Under its lower edge and both tails, a soft shadow of deep indigo (about #0B0A2E at 65%), dropped about 6 units in the 400 box and blurred about 4, so the cells just beneath the ribbon sink into dusk and climb back to full neon a little further out. The letters, their gold and magenta edge and the dark band itself stay exactly as they are; only the wall under them darkens. Hyperspace is stacked planes at different depths, and the name hovering one plane in front of the tunnel, like a tablet the entity holds up to you, also gives it more of the wide dark halo the owner asked for.

The four eye-bubbles rising from the snout at upper left (the largest near 160,160 in the 800 px render, shrinking down toward 90,290): right now each is a flat navy disc behind its eye. I see them turn into lenses. Inside each, behind the eye, a dim copy of the honeycomb drawn about 1.7 times larger with a slight swirl, as if seen through curved glass; along the lower-right rim a thin rainbow fringe crescent, red on the outside to violet on the inside, about 0.5 wide in the 400 box; a short cream highlight arc at the upper left. The inside stays dark so the eye stays bright and centered. Every breath the angel lets go becomes a window into a deeper level of the tunnel, and the rainbow fringe rhymes with the prism fin: wherever light passes through the entity, it splits.
visions.keep: The turbine sweep of the outer eye-petals against the upward-flicking middle ring (Vision 1's very first offer, taken at last, and the mandala finally turns); the beaded magenta and cyan collar with its eye pendant slung low at the belly edge (moving it down off the mouth was right: it reads as a presence, not a smile); the pale striped diamond that reads as an angelfish at 240 and 160 px; the spiral-web teardrop eyes, almond third eye, violet brows, chevron nose and falling-jewel mouth; the cheek whorls winding down to gold points; the tail corridor with its white-gold waist and little star; the pastel oil-on-water feathers with eyes down each quill; the domed skin; the void honeycomb through the black bars; the cream angelfish catchlights; the clear prism fin; the golden procession facing in; the honeycomb dimming toward the entity with the corner eyes shut; the beaded cords curling away from the S; and the swallowtail ribbon with the bold cream SavesFish standing off it like carved neon, gold and magenta edge, calm dark backing, nothing touching the letters. Vision 6's three offers (a cool moon lamp in the lower pocket by the tail, tapering fiddlehead coral, a soft glow under the aura) are still open; I have not repeated them here.
